title: Normalization covers of regular surfaces and their completed local degrees
statement: Let $Y$ be an integral regular excellent Noetherian scheme of dimension $2$ [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-regular-scheme], [def-exc-excellent-ring], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-weil-pbc-krull-dimension-ring]. Let $F=k(Y)$ and let $K/F$ be a finite field extension of degree $d$ [def-sc-function-field], [def-pc-field-extension]. Let $\pi:X\to Y$ be the normalization of $Y$ in $K$ [def-fin-normalization-extension]. Then $X$ is integral, normal, excellent, Noetherian, and of dimension $2$, its function field is $K$, and $\pi$ is finite and surjective [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-surjective-morphism]. For every closed point $x\in X$ with $\dim\mathcal O_{X,x}=2$, put $y=\pi(x)$, $R=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$ and $S=\mathcal O_{X,x}$. The point $y$ is closed and has $\dim R=2$. The map of completions $\widehat R\to\widehat S$ is finite and injective, $\widehat R$ is a complete regular Noetherian local domain, $\widehat S$ is a complete normal Noetherian local domain of dimension $2$, and $[\operatorname{Frac}(\widehat S):\operatorname{Frac}(\widehat R)]\leq d$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. Moreover, suppose $C\subseteq D$ are Noetherian normal domains, $D$ is finite over $C$, $F=\operatorname{Frac}(C)$ and $K=\operatorname{Frac}(D)$, and $Y\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ is a proper morphism inducing the identity on $F$. Then there is an induced proper morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}D$ inducing the identity on $K$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], [def-weil-proper-morphism].

source.place: The normalization-cover and completed-degree comparison used in Tag 0BGN, resolve-lemma-resolve-complete, intermediate-field paragraph. Finiteness of normalization: morphisms.tex Tag 035S (morphisms-lemma-nagata-normalization), with the Japanese affine description; normal surfaces: properties.tex Tag 0B3D. Completions: algebra.tex Tag 0325 and more-algebra.tex Tags 07NY, 0C23. This is the local degree comparison, not an existence theorem for regular models. The completed-degree bound uses the normal-surface Cohen-Macaulay property and algebra.tex Tag 00R4 (algebra-lemma-CM-over-regular-flat): the finite normalization is locally free of generic rank d, and its completed semilocal algebra splits into factors of ranks at most d.

proof.text: On a nonempty affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $Y$, the function field is $F=\operatorname{Frac}(A)$ by [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction]. Put $B=\overline A^{\,K}$. By [lem-exc-quasi-excellent-nagata], $A$ is Nagata; [lem-weil-pbc-nagata-domain-n2] and [def-weil-pbc-japanese-domain] give that $B$ is a finite $A$-module. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-closure-finite-extension-normal], $B$ is a normal domain with fraction field $K$. The affine descriptions of [def-fin-normalization-extension] identify $\pi^{-1}V$ with $\operatorname{Spec}B$. Thus $\pi$ is finite by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], and it is surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-lying-over], since $A\subseteq B$ is integral.

The affine pieces $\operatorname{Spec}B$ have common generic point with residue field $K$ (the inclusions into $K$ agree on overlaps), so their glued scheme $X$ is integral and has function field $K$. Their local rings are normal domains by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-normal-domain]. Each $B$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-noetherian] and excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent]: a finite list of $A$-module generators also generates $B$ as an $A$-algebra. A finite affine cover of $Y$ gives a finite such cover of $X$, hence $X$ is Noetherian. To compute dimension on each piece, [lem-weil-pbc-integral-extension-dimension] gives $\dim B\leq\dim A$. Conversely lift the bottom prime of any finite chain in $A$ by [lem-weil-pbc-integral-injective-lying-over] and lift successive inclusions by [pqf-lem-going-up]. Distinct contractions force distinct lifted primes, so $\dim B\geq\dim A$. Applying [lem-pc-dimension-affine-open-cover] to these two covers gives $\dim X=\dim Y=2$.

Fix a closed $x$ as in the statement. Since $\pi$ is a closed map by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres], $y=\pi(x)$ is closed. Choose the affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ above containing $y$, write $\pi^{-1}V=\operatorname{Spec}B$, and let $\mathfrak q$ and $\mathfrak p=\mathfrak q\cap A$ represent $x$ and $y$. By [lem-weil-pbc-affine-open-stalk-localization], $R=A_{\mathfrak p}$ and $S=B_{\mathfrak q}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-integral-incomparability], contracting a length-two prime chain ending at $\mathfrak q$ gives a strict length-two chain ending at $\mathfrak p$. Thus $2=\dim S\leq\dim R\leq\dim Y=2$. The ring $R$ is regular by the hypothesis on $Y$, while $S$ is normal by Step 2. No finiteness of $R\to S$ is asserted.

The rings $R,S$ are excellent by [lem-exc-finite-type-localization-excellent] and Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. Their completions are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-adic-completion-noetherian], local with the extended maximal ideals by [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-local-ring], and complete by [lem-weil-pbc-module-completion-complete] applied with module the ring itself (the maximal ideals are finitely generated). By [lem-weil-pbc-completion-dimension] their dimensions are two. By [lem-weil-pbc-completion-regular-local], $\widehat R$ is regular; it is a domain by [lem-sc-regular-local-domain]. For $S$, excellence supplies the G-ring condition [def-exc-excellent-ring], so [lem-weil-pbc-g-ring-completion-regular] makes $S\to\widehat S$ flat with geometrically regular Noetherian fibres. Those fibres are regular by taking the identity field extension in [def-weil-pbc-g-ring], hence normal by [lem-weil-pbc-regular-ring-normal]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-flat-normal-fibres-noetherian-normal] to deduce that $\widehat S$ is normal. A local normal ring is a normal domain by [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring] applied at its maximal ideal.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-completion-finite-extension] to the finite map $A\subseteq B$ at $\mathfrak p$. It gives the canonical $\widehat R$-algebra isomorphism
$E:=\widehat R\otimes_A B\simeq\prod_{\mathfrak q'\mid\mathfrak p}\widehat{B_{\mathfrak q'}}$.
In particular $\widehat S$ is the factor indexed by $\mathfrak q$. If $b_1,\ldots,b_t$ generate $B$ over $A$, the elements $1\otimes b_j$ generate $E$ over $\widehat R$; their projections generate $\widehat S$. Thus the canonical completion map $\widehat R\to\widehat S$ is finite. Its identification as the map induced by $R\to S$ is part of the cited statement.

source.place: Tag 07N9 (lemma-completion-finite-extension), canonical algebra structures and product decomposition.

proof.text: Choose an $F$-basis $v_1,\ldots,v_d$ of $K$. Express the finitely many generators $b_j$ of $B$ in this basis. A common nonzero denominator $a\in A$ for their coordinates defines an injective $A$-linear map $u:B\to A^d$, sending $b$ to $a$ times its coordinate vector: coordinates of every $A$-linear combination of the $b_j$ lie in $a^{-1}A^d$, and zero coordinates imply $b=0$. This is just finite linear algebra and clearing the finitely many displayed denominators; it does not assume $B$ free.

source.place: Tag 0BGN (lemma-resolve-complete), omitted completed-degree comparison: explicit coordinate argument for its generic-degree bound.

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-local-completion-faithfully-flat], $R\to\widehat R$ is faithfully flat, hence flat. Localize the injection $u$ of Step 6 at $\mathfrak p$ using [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact]. Tensor it over $R$ with the flat module $\widehat R$; [lem-trf-flat-tensor-preserves-injection] gives an injection $E\hookrightarrow\widehat R^d$. In the product of Step 5, insertion in the $\mathfrak q$ coordinate is an injective $\widehat R$-linear map $\widehat S\hookrightarrow E$. Consequently $\widehat S$ is torsion free over the domain $\widehat R$. If a nonzero $r\in\widehat R$ mapped to zero in $\widehat S$, it would annihilate $1\in\widehat S$, contradicting torsion freeness and the fact that $\widehat S$ is a nonzero domain. The completion map is therefore injective.

source.place: Tags 00MC (lemma-completion-faithfully-flat), 00CS (proposition-localization-exact); Mathlib Module.Flat.lTensor_preserves_injective_linearMap, used for the explicit coordinate injection.

proof.text: Put $Q=\operatorname{Frac}(\widehat R)$. Localizing the injection $\widehat S\hookrightarrow\widehat R^d$ of Step 7 using [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] gives an injection $H:=(\widehat R\setminus\{0\})^{-1}\widehat S\hookrightarrow Q^d$. Since $\widehat R\to\widehat S$ is injective and $\widehat S$ is a domain, $H$ is a nonzero domain; it has $Q$-dimension at most $d$ (a linearly independent family maps to one in $Q^d$). By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-domain-is-field], $H$ is a field. It contains $\widehat S$ and is contained in $\operatorname{Frac}(\widehat S)$, so every quotient of two elements of $\widehat S$ already lies in $H$. Thus $H=\operatorname{Frac}(\widehat S)$ and $[\operatorname{Frac}(\widehat S):Q]\leq d$, with the field map induced by the completion map as required.

source.place: Tag 0BGN (lemma-resolve-complete), intermediate-field paragraph: completed local degree is smaller than the original induction degree; explicit fraction-field comparison.

proof.text: For the final assertion let $f:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ be the given proper morphism. On each nonempty affine $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq Y$, the map $C\to A\subseteq F$ is the prescribed inclusion, by [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction] and the generic-point hypothesis. Every $z\in D\subseteq K$ is integral over $C$ because $D$ is finite over $C$; equivalently it satisfies a monic polynomial over $C$ (the finite-implies-integral clause of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-algebra-is-integral]). The same polynomial has coefficients in $A$, so $z\in\overline A^{\,K}=B$. These inclusions $D\to B$ commute with restrictions, all being inclusions in $K$. Using the affine normalization description [def-fin-normalization-extension], they therefore glue to $h:X\to\operatorname{Spec}D$ over $\operatorname{Spec}C$. At the generic point the induced map is $D\subseteq K$, hence its extension to fraction fields is the identity on $K$.

source.place: Tag 0BGN (lemma-resolve-complete), intermediate-field diagram; affine description of normalization in the finite field extension.

proof.text: The composite $X\xrightarrow{\pi}Y\xrightarrow{f}\operatorname{Spec}C$ is proper: $\pi$ is finite by Step 1, hence proper by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-proper], and [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition] applies to $\pi,f$. The morphism $\operatorname{Spec}D\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ is finite, hence separated by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-closed-map-finite-fibres]. Apply [lemma-nagata-proper-to-separated-target] to the triangle $X\xrightarrow{h}\operatorname{Spec}D\to\operatorname{Spec}C$ constructed in Step 9. It proves $h$ proper, completing the last assertion.
